id: biblical.daniel

current_text_paths:

uncertainty: "Most scholars date Daniel's final apocalyptic composition and redaction to ca. 167-164 BCE, during the persecution under Antiochus IV, while the court tales in chapters 1-6 likely circulated earlier, perhaps in the third century BCE. This range dates the underlying Hebrew-Aramaic work, not the King James English translation first published in 1611 and commonly presented in its 1769 standardized form."

id: biblical.ezekiel
title: Book of Ezekiel

culture: ancient_israelite_prophetic_literature

current_text_paths:
  - texts/public-domain/biblical/project-gutenberg/ezekiel-kjv.md
uncertainty: "The book dates Ezekiel's prophetic activity to ca. 593-571 BCE, and much of its material is commonly associated with that exilic setting. Its literary shaping and later additions may have continued among Ezekiel's followers into the early Persian period, so the date of its final form is uncertain. The English text here is the King James Version of 1611, generally encountered in its standardized 1769 form."

id: biblical.isaiah
title: Book of Isaiah
tradition_cluster: biblical
culture: ancient_israelite
region: ancient_near_east_levant

  start_year: -740

current_text_paths:
  - texts/public-domain/biblical/project-gutenberg/isaiah-kjv.md
uncertainty: "Isaiah contains material associated with the eighth-century BCE prophet, exilic material commonly dated to the sixth century BCE, and post-exilic additions and redaction extending into the Persian period. The boundaries and dates of these layers remain disputed, so this range represents the collection's broad compositional development rather than a single act of authorship. The text presented here is the 1611 King James English translation in its later standardized form, not an ancient manuscript witness."

id: biblical.book_of_job

uncertainty: "Job is a composite work whose poetic dialogues, prose framework, and later passages may derive from different periods; many scholars place its principal composition or final literary shaping in the sixth to fourth centuries BCE. The broader range reflects substantial linguistic and redactional uncertainty, while the present English text is the 1611 King James translation as standardized in 1769."

id: biblical.psalms

uncertainty: "The individual psalms vary widely in date: some may preserve monarchic-period material, while many are exilic or post-exilic, and the Psalter's final arrangement developed during the Second Temple period. Precise dates and traditional Davidic attributions remain disputed; the English text presented here is the 1611 King James translation, commonly printed in its standardized 1769 form."
